neighbours.label: a token inside the namespace/version/key syntax of XML, SPARQL or code (the '.' in a version like 1.1.0 in a schema URL, a quoted key, a ?variable)
quiet:
The web feature service returned a list of map layers for the region,
and the client drew them on the screen in a few seconds.

The access policy compares two strings and allows the request
only when the user's department matches the resource owner.

The query looks for every activity and the time it ended,
and it skips the activities that have no recorded end time.

The blog app stores each post with a title of up to two hundred
characters, and the admin page lists them by date.

The parser reads the document and passes each element to the handler,
which counts how many ids it has seen so far.

The schema describes what an order looks like: a customer,
a list of items and a delivery address.

The query finds every person in the dataset together with their name
and prints them in alphabetical order.

The application context creates the beans at startup
and wires them together before the first request arrives.

notes: card only; top examples mix SPARQL ?variables, quoted Django keys, version dots in XML schema URLs and one Bible verse; the - pole is ' same' in 'of the same name'
